historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 5-year average revenue growth (FY2027-FY2031: 17/9/7/5.5/4.5) anchored on the FY2027 guidance midpoint; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because book equity ($1.35B against a $43B market cap) is an artefact of buybacks exceeding earnings, and the FCF 3-year CAGR is off the FY2023 trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.5% and EPS 5yr CAGR 14.3% diverge >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 3.8%: EPS growth came from margin expansion (GAAP op margin 13.7% FY2021 -> 24.2% FY2026) and a 226M -> 200M share count, not from top-line growth; equity growth is off a buyback-depleted $685M base. Neither is a forward revenue proxy.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding - interest income): FY21 923, FY22 659, FY23 403, FY24 934, FY25 641, FY26 1,237. The owner 5yr CAGR (6.0%) is materially below the reported 5yr CAGR (9.8%): SBC plus withholding grew from $239M (FY21) to $519M (FY26), so a growing share of reported FCF growth was paid for in stock. The 3yr owner CAGR (45%) is off the FY2023 trough (cash taxes 386 + withholding 84 on a $868M reported base) and is not representative; FY2026 reported FCF also carries an estimated $130-190M working-capital tailwind.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 at the raised guidance midpoint (+17%), decaying to mid-single-digit growth by FY2030 as the all-flash refresh and AI pull-forward normalise; adj EBITDA 34% -> 33%; SBC all-in 7.3% -> 6.0%; cash tax 24% -> 22%; terminal 2.5% at a 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Beat-and-raise continues (+21% FY2027), Novus opens a durable neocloud/GPU-cloud leg, double-digit growth through FY2029, adj EBITDA to 36%, SBC to 5.5%; terminal 3.0% capped at 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI pull-forward fades (+13% FY2027), capex digestion (flat FY2028, -3% FY2029), Pure share gains and NAND cost squeeze compress adj EBITDA to 28.5-29%, growth reverts to the company's ~2% long-run history; terminal 2.0%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NetApp is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow: reported FCF less stock-based compensation (including the cash tax withheld on net-share settlement) less interest income, with the diluted share count held flat because SBC is expensed. The forward margin is built from components (adj EBITDA, SBC, D&A, cash tax, capex, working capital on revenue growth) rather than carried from FY2026, whose reported FCF held a working-capital tailwind. The three scenarios differ on one axis above all: whether the FY2027 AI/all-flash surge is the start of a multi-year leg (bull), a spike that decays to the storage market's mid-single-digit trend (base), or a pull-forward followed by digestion (bear). The terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF because the company's own history is a ~1% revenue CAGR with cyclical troughs; the street basis is reported alongside so the reader can see how much of the market price depends on treating SBC as non-cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI capex sustainability: FY2027 guidance (+17%) and Q1's +30% are driven by neocloud/GPU-cloud and all-flash demand; a hyperscaler/neocloud spending pause would hit growth and margins in the same year
Competitive share loss in all-flash arrays to Pure Storage and Dell, which would show up first in product gross margin and then in growth
NAND/flash and component cost inflation compressing product gross margin (70% FY2026) while pricing is contested
Hyperscaler disintermediation of third-party storage over the 10-year horizon, which caps the terminal growth and multiple

SBC treatment: house IV expenses $519M/yr (7.5% of revenue) of SBC and withholding; the street basis, which treats it as non-cash, is materially higher and is closer to how the market prices the shares
Cash tax: the model assumes Section 174 relief brings the cash rate from 26% to 22%; if it stays at 26% the base IV is lower by roughly 5%
Price is at the 52-week high after a ~130% re-rating; the valuation is on fundamentals and the stock's momentum is not an input

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 93.69-216.81
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1002047): FY2026 10-K filed 2026-06-05 (FY ended 2026-04-24) for FY0 flows; Q1 FY2027 10-Q filed 2026-09-02 (quarter ended 2026-07-31) for cash, short-term investments, debt and the diluted share count; NTAP_Metrics.csv / NTAP.duckdb metrics_normalized for the history and KPIs (cash_taxes, equity_award_taxes, interest_income, buybacks, deferred_revenue)
data_sources.qualitative: NTAP_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q1 FY2027 results and raised FY2027 guidance (revenue $7.975-8.225B, non-GAAP EPS $9.73-10.03), Insight 2026 / Novus launch, competitive position vs Dell and Pure Storage

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $382M add-back plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $137M (financing). NetApp publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the method; the withholding line is the vest-date cost of net-share settlement and ran $127M/$199M/$137M in FY24/25/26.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 repurchases $950M (financing outflow); Q1 FY2027 $200M. Diluted count fell 203M -> 200M over FY2026. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded, and the cash that funds it is already charged as SBC.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average 200.0M for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q, filed 2026-09-02); basic 196M; cover-page 196.4M at 2026-08-28. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet 2026-07-31 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q): cash $1,573M + short-term investments $2,003M = $3,576M liquid; LongTermDebt $2,488M (current $550M + non-current $1,938M; no commercial paper). Net cash $1,088M. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt of $3,038M (and FY2025's $3,985M) double-counts the current portion of long-term debt, the same XBRL artefact seen on KEYS/NDSN; do not use it. Operating lease liabilities ($246M at FY26) are excluded: lease cost is an opex line inside EBITDA under US GAAP (single lease treatment).
inputs.owner_fcf_note: FY2026 owner FCF = reported FCF 1,869 - SBC incl. withholding 519 - interest income 113 = 1,237 (17.9% margin). Interest income is stripped although net cash (1.09B) is ~0.9x the owner-FCF base, because the forward component build is unlevered and the anchor should match; the ~$60M/yr of interest expense inside reported OCF is deliberately NOT added back, so the anchor is slightly conservative. Component reconstruction of FY2026 (EBIT 1,674 - cash tax 435 + D&A 200 - capex 198 - withholding 137 = 1,104) implies ~$130-190M of FY2026 reported FCF was working-capital timing (OCF rose $561M on NI +$90M); the forward build starts from components, not from the 1,237 margin.
inputs.cash_tax_note: Cash taxes paid: FY24 357 (29% of EBIT), FY25 412 (31%), FY26 435 (26%). The excess over the ~21% GAAP/non-GAAP rate is Section 174 R&D capitalisation; OBBBA (Jul-2025) restores domestic R&D expensing from FY2026 onward, so the cash rate is ramped 24% -> 22% rather than carried at 26% or dropped straight to 21% (Pillar Two / GILTI keep a floor above the headline rate).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10%; $2.5B notes at ~5% refinancing cost after tax ~4%; debt ~5.5% of market capital at $215 -> WACC ~9.7%, used 9.5% in all three scenarios. Risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not through per-scenario WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (liability $246M at FY2026) are an opex charge inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Single treatment: cost in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: None; NetApp has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company, enterprise storage software/hardware; first valuation of this ticker, no memory entry). Not a bank/REIT/LIC; US filer, USD, no NCI, no excluded assets, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md does not apply. 10-year horizon because FY2027 carries a +17% AI/all-flash growth spike that must decelerate to a mature rate before capitalising; a 5-year cut would capitalise a 5-6% growth year. Adj EBITDA is defined as GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC (pre-SBC, SBC charged separately as sbc_pct_path incl. withholding taxes); FY2026 actual 32.6%, Q1 FY2027 30.4% (Q1 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter; +2pp YoY). FY2027 base revenue growth is the 2026-09-02 raised guidance midpoint ($8.10B, +17.0%); Q1 FY2027 ran +30% and the guide implies Q2-Q4 +13%, so the midpoint is not aggressive. PERIOD LABELS: the Metrics CSV labels quarters by calendar end-date, so the 'Q3 2026' row (rev $2,025M, ending 2026-07-31) is NetApp's fiscal Q1 FY2027; annual FY rows are fiscally correct and are the anchors used here. Terminal cap 15x (not 20x): a hardware-exposed vendor with a 14-year revenue CAGR of ~0.8% (FY2012 6,233 -> FY2026 6,925) and two prior capex-digestion down-cycles (FY2013-16, FY2019-20) should not be capitalised as a mature compounder.

bear.narrative: FY2027 finishes below the bottom of the guide (+13%) as the AI-storage pull-forward fades in H2, then a capex-digestion cycle like FY2013-16 and FY2019-20: flat FY2028, -3% FY2029 as neocloud/GPU-cloud buyers pause, Pure Storage keeps taking all-flash share, and hyperscalers lean on their native storage tiers. NAND price inflation and discounting compress adj EBITDA to 28.5% before recovering to 29%, SBC stays sticky at 7-7.5% on a shrinking base, and the business reverts to the ~2% growth of its own 14-year history.

base.narrative: FY2027 at the raised guidance midpoint (+17%), then the AI/all-flash spike decays to mid-single digits by FY2030 and GDP-plus by FY2033 as the AFA refresh wave passes. Adj EBITDA margin ~34% in the leverage years (Q1 FY27 non-GAAP op margin 32%), settling to 33% as NAND cost inflation and Pure/Dell pricing take back some of the mix benefit. SBC all-in glides 7.3% -> 6.0%. Cash tax normalises 24% -> 22% as Section 174 relief lands. Capex ~3% (Q1 FY27 ran 5%, treated as timing). WC captures 10% of incremental revenue (deferred revenue 33% of sales offset by hardware receivables/inventory).

bull.narrative: The Q1 FY27 beat-and-raise pattern repeats: FY2027 lands above the top of the guide (+21%) as all-flash (+47% in Q1) keeps compounding and Novus wins real neocloud/GPU-as-a-service deployments, giving NetApp a second growth leg that holds double-digit growth through FY2029. First-party hyperscaler services (ANF, FSx for ONTAP, GCNV) lift the recurring mix, operating leverage carries adj EBITDA to 36%, and SBC falls to 5.5% of a much larger revenue base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because roughly a third of the current growth story rests on AI/GPU-infrastructure capex that has a boom-bust profile, NetApp is a hardware-exposed vendor with two capex-digestion down-cycles in its own 14-year record, and Pure Storage is closing the all-flash share gap. Bull lowered to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: sustained AI capex, Novus adoption by a customer segment NetApp has never served at scale, and all-flash share held against Pure and Dell. No going-concern or balance-sheet risk (net cash), so the bear is a margin/growth case, not a solvency case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
